title: Semilinear action and projective geometric integrality of the Stein base
statement:
Let $k$ be a field, let $T$ be a normal projective geometrically integral finite-type $k$-scheme, let $B$ be an integral projective finite-type $k$-scheme, and let $f:T\to B$ be a dominant $k$-morphism. Let a finite group $H$ act semilinearly on $T$, $B$ and $k$, and suppose $f$ is equivariant. Put $E=k(T)$ and $F=k(B)$, with the inclusion induced by $f$. For the Stein scheme $Y=\underline{\operatorname{Spec}}_B(f_*\mathcal O_T)$ and its evaluation factorization $T\xrightarrow{g}Y\xrightarrow{q}B$, the scheme $Y$ is normal, projective and geometrically integral of finite type over $k$, $q$ is finite, dominant and H-projective, and $g$ is proper, dominant and H-projective with geometrically connected fibres. There is a unique semilinear $H$-action on $Y$ making both $g$ and $q$ equivariant. For each affine open $W\subseteq B$, its action from $q^{-1}W$ to $q^{-1}(hW)$ is the spectrum of pullback on $\Gamma(f^{-1}(hW),\mathcal O_T)\to\Gamma(f^{-1}W,\mathcal O_T)$. Inside $E$ one has $k(Y)=L=\{x\in E:x\text{ is algebraic over }F\}$; $L/F$ is finite and $L$ is algebraically closed in $E$.

The notions used are [def-weil-field], [def-pc-integral-scheme], [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], [def-weil-proper-morphism], [def-kun-projective], [def-sc-function-field], [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], [def-weil-affine-spectrum], [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible], [def-weil-relative-algebraic-closure], [def-sfb-dominant-function-field-map]. Normal means that every local ring is an integrally closed domain. A projective morphism here means an H-projective morphism: it admits a closed immersion into a finite-dimensional projective space over its target. A semilinear $H$-action means actions by scheme automorphisms and by field automorphisms of $k$, with the structure morphisms equivariant; faithfulness is not assumed. A birational morphism here identifies the function fields and is an isomorphism over a dense open of the target.

source.place: Tag 03H0, theorem-stein-factorization-Noetherian; de Jong Lemma 5.2 proof, printed p.613, induced action on the Stein scheme and geometric integrality over the original field. Equivariant section maps and projectivity are the arguments of returned curve-pencil steps 12--14.

proof.text: First regard all morphisms as ordinary scheme morphisms. Since $B/k$ is H-projective, projective-implies-proper makes it proper, hence separated over $k$. Apply the finite-constant projective graph lemma with constant extension $k/k$, projective source $T$ and separated target $B$. It makes the given $f:T\to B$ H-projective and proper. Its dominance is a hypothesis. No equivariant projective embedding is required: H-projective here is the finite-projective-space convention, not an extra linearization condition.

source.place: Tag 01WC (lemma-locally-projective-proper); Tag 0C4Q (lemma-projective-permanence), closed graph proof, specialized to projective spaces and the identity constant extension

proof.text: The scheme $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is Noetherian: its sole affine chart has only the ideals $(0)$ and $(1)$. Finite type over a Noetherian scheme therefore makes $T$ and $B$ Noetherian. Apply the normal Noetherian Stein-model lemma to $f$. It gives precisely the canonical $Y=\underline{\operatorname{Spec}}_B(f_*\mathcal O_T)$ and evaluation factorization, with $Y$ integral and normal, $q$ finite and dominant, and $g$ proper and dominant with geometrically connected fibres. For affine $W=\operatorname{Spec}A\subset B$, write $R_W=\Gamma(f^{-1}W,\mathcal O_T)$: its charts are $q^{-1}W=\operatorname{Spec}R_W$, with $R_W$ finite over $A$ and evaluation pullback the identity of $R_W$. These are the maps specified in the item.

source.place: Tag 03H0 (theorem-stein-factorization-Noetherian), with morphisms.tex Tag 035L (lemma-normal-normalization); Noetherian setup from morphisms.tex Tag 01T6 (lemma-finite-type-noetherian)

proof.text: Apply the normal Stein constant-field lemma to the same proper dominant $f$ of integral finite-type $k$-schemes. Its scheme is this same relative spectrum and its map is this same evaluation map, so no choice of factorization is being identified merely birationally. It supplies finite type of $Y/k$ and, through the pullback inclusion into $E$, the equality $k(Y)=L=\{x\in E:x\text{ is algebraic over }F\}$, finiteness of $L/F$, and algebraic closedness of $L$ in $E$.

source.place: Tag 03H0 (theorem-stein-factorization-Noetherian); normal Stein constant-field lemma, whose explicit evaluation and function-field clauses are used

proof.text: Apply finite-over-projective to $Y\xrightarrow{q}B\to\operatorname{Spec}k$. The outer base is affine Noetherian, so the lemma gives a global closed immersion $Y\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^N_k$, not merely local projectivity on $B$. Thus $Y$ is projective over $k$ and hence proper and separated over $k$. Apply the finite-constant projective graph lemma with constant extension $k/k$ first to the projective source $Y$ and separated target $B$, then to the projective source $T$ and separated target $Y$. It gives H-projectivity of $q$ and $g$. The properness and all dominance and fibre assertions already obtained are retained.

Since $T$ is integral and geometrically irreducible, the generic-point criterion makes $\operatorname{Spec}E$ geometrically irreducible over $k$. The subextension lemma applied to $k\subseteq L\subseteq E$ makes $\operatorname{Spec}L$ geometrically irreducible. The same generic-point criterion, now for the integral $Y$ and its function field $L$, proves that $Y$ is geometrically irreducible over the original field $k$. The criteria impose no perfectness assumption on $k$.

source.place: Tag 054Q (lemma-geometrically-irreducible-function-field), equivalence (1) and (2); algebra.tex Tag 037N (lemma-subalgebra-geometrically-irreducible), part (1)

proof.text: The proper $g$ is quasi-compact. It is scheme-theoretically dominant, as follows directly from the section embeddings for integral schemes. For a nonempty open $V\subseteq Y$, dominance makes $g^{-1}V$ nonempty. Pullback $\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_Y)\to\Gamma(g^{-1}V,\mathcal O_T)$ commutes with germs at the generic points and with the field injection $L\hookrightarrow E$; the injection of $\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_Y)$ into $L$ therefore makes this pullback injective. On the empty open there is nothing to check. These injections say exactly that $\mathcal O_Y\to g_*\mathcal O_T$ has zero kernel. Apply geometric-reducedness descent along a quasi-compact schematically dominant map to $g$: $T$ is geometrically reduced by hypothesis, so $Y$ is geometrically reduced. For every field extension $k'/k$, $Y_{k'}$ is reduced by this descent and irreducible by Step 5. It is nonempty: an affine neighbourhood of the generic point has a nonzero $k$-algebra $A$, and $A\otimes_k k'$ contains the injected copy of $A$ (extend a $k$-basis containing $1$). Thus the reduced-and-irreducible criterion gives integrality of every $Y_{k'}$.

source.place: Tags 081I (lemma-flat-base-change-scheme-theoretic-image), 056B (lemma-scheme-theoretic-image-reduced); section embeddings as in properties.tex Tag 01ON and morphisms.tex Tag 01RV; integral criterion properties.tex Tag 01ON

proof.text: Write $\mathcal A=f_*\mathcal O_T$. On the affine basis of $B$, evaluation identifies $\mathcal A$ with $q_*\mathcal O_Y$: both section rings are $R_W$, compatibly with restriction. Fix $h\in H$ and write $Y_h=(Y,h_B\circ q)$ and $Y_0=(Y,q)$ as schemes over $B$. The former is affine: the inverse image of an affine $V$ is $q^{-1}(h_B^{-1}V)$, an affine Stein chart. Its direct-image algebra is $\mathcal A_h(V)=\mathcal A(h_B^{-1}V)$, with structure map $\mathcal O_B(V)\xrightarrow{h_B^\sharp}\mathcal O_B(h_B^{-1}V)\to\mathcal A(h_B^{-1}V)$. Pullback by $h_T$ gives a restriction-compatible map $\varphi_h:\mathcal A\to\mathcal A_h$. Explicitly, for $r\in\mathcal O_B(V)$, equivariance gives $h_T^\sharp(f^\sharp r)=f^\sharp(h_B^\sharp r)$, so this is an $\mathcal O_B$-algebra map. The affine-algebra anti-equivalence sends it contravariantly to a $B$-morphism $a_h:Y_h\to Y_0$, hence an underlying scheme map $Y\to Y$ with $q a_h=h_B q$. Over $V=h_BW$, its source and target are respectively $q^{-1}W$ and $q^{-1}(h_BW)$, and its formula is $\operatorname{Spec}(h_T^\sharp:R_{h_BW}\to R_W)$. The restriction clause supplies compatibility on overlaps, without requiring affine intersections.

source.place: Tag 01SA (lemma-affine-equivalence-algebras), including base change compatibility; constructions.tex Tag 01LX (lemma-spec-properties), affine section formula and open restriction

proof.text: On $f^{-1}W$, the two maps $a_h g$ and $g h_T$ have target $q^{-1}(h_BW)=\operatorname{Spec}R_{h_BW}$. Their section maps are both $h_T^\sharp:R_{h_BW}\to R_W$, since evaluation pullback is the identity. The affine-spectrum adjunction and gluing of morphisms therefore give $a_h g=g h_T$. Conversely, any $b_h$ satisfying these two equivariance equations maps $q^{-1}W$ into $q^{-1}(h_BW)$; pulling its section map back along $g|_{f^{-1}W}$, whose pullback on sections is the identity, forces $b_h^\sharp=h_T^\sharp$. The same adjunction and gluing imply $b_h=a_h$. Both $a_1$ and the identity satisfy these equations; and both $a_h a_j$ and $a_{hj}$ satisfy them, since $h_Tj_T=(hj)_T$ and $h_Bj_B=(hj)_B$. Uniqueness gives $a_1=1$ and $a_h a_j=a_{hj}$; in particular $a_{h^{-1}}$ is inverse to $a_h$. Finally, if $p_B:B\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ and $p_Y=p_Bq$, then $p_Ya_h=p_Bh_Bq=h_kp_Bq=h_kp_Y$. This proves semilinearity, the group laws, both equivariances, and uniqueness of the action. Faithfulness and a bound on the group order were never used.

tool_uses.why: Ordinary properness and separatedness of projective schemes; projectivity is used as a generic scheme-theoretic tool.
Generic scheme-theoretic finiteness tool for the normal Stein construction; no unit route is replaced.
Only its affine-base case is used, over Spec k, to obtain projectivity of the finite Stein cover; no result of the unit supplies this projective embedding.
Generic-point characterization of geometric irreducibility used twice as a generic tool over the original field.
Geometric irreducibility passes to the intermediate function field; a generic algebra tool, not a replacement of the alteration argument.
Injection of sections into the function field verifies schematic dominance explicitly.
Generic descent of geometric reducedness from T to its schematically dominated Stein base, with no perfect-field hypothesis.
Restriction-compatible affine-algebra anti-equivalence constructs the action from the displayed twisted algebra map.
Maps into each affine Stein chart are determined by their section map; used to prove equivariance and uniqueness.
Equality of morphisms is checked on the affine-base open covers; this is a generic gluing tool.

Step 6 (changed): sections inject into L and then E, so g is schematically dominant and quasi-compact; dominant descent gives geometric reducedness; the newly written nonemptiness of Y_{k'} (A tensor k' contains A) and the reduced-irreducible criterion give geometric integrality. Step 8: equivariance, uniqueness, group law and semilinearity follow from the affine adjunction and gluing; I verified each identity.
